2027-06-28.title: Saint Irenaeus, Bishop, Martyr and Doctor of the Church
readings: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?
The Lord is kind and merciful
Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head
2027-06-28.alt: Memorial of St Irenaeus. Readings of Monday of the Thirteenth Week in Ordinary Time (Year I); proper readings from the Common of Pastors or of Doctors may be used. Liturgical colour: red. This evening the Vigil Mass of the Solemnity of Sts Peter and Paul is celebrated, with its own readings: Acts 3:1–10; Psalm 19:1–4 (Lectionary 19:2–5); Galatians 1:11–20; John 21:15–19.
2027-06-28.verse: Then Abraham came near and said, “Will you indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
theo: The three visitors leave Abraham's tent and look toward Sodom, and the Lord shares a secret with his friend: “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?” Abraham has been chosen so that through him “all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,” and so that he may teach his children “to keep the way of the LORD by doing righteousness and justice.” A man with such a calling must learn how God judges. “How great is the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah and how very grave their sin!” The word outcry is the cry of victims; the Bible later names the sins of Sodom as pride, excess of food, prosperous ease and neglect of the poor and needy (Ezekiel 16:49), together with the violence against strangers told in the next chapter. God says he will “go down and see,” like a just judge who examines before he sentences. Then comes one of the most remarkable prayers in the Old Testament. “Abraham remained standing before the LORD.” He comes near and asks: “Will you indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked?” He does not ask only that the righteous be spared; he asks that the whole city be forgiven for their sake. Six times he presses, from fifty to forty-five, to forty, thirty, twenty, ten, each time with deep humility, “I who am but dust and ashes,” and with great boldness: “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?” Each time God agrees. The story teaches that the presence of a few righteous people can protect a whole community, and that God is more ready to forgive than we are to ask. Abraham stopped at ten. The prophets would go further (Jeremiah 5:1), and St Paul would see the fulfilment in one righteous man: “by the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous” (Romans 5:19). The Psalm sings the heart of the God Abraham was speaking to: “He does not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities.”

In the Gospel two men offer to follow Jesus, and he answers each with a hard saying. To an eager scribe who promises, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go,” Jesus says, “Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.” Following him is not a comfortable career; it means sharing the life of a homeless wanderer. To a disciple who asks first to bury his father, Jesus says, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.” The words are shocking, for burying one's parents was a sacred duty in Israel. Jesus is not teaching contempt for parents; he is saying that the call of the kingdom comes before everything, even the holiest human duties, and that those who do not follow him are, in a sense, the dead. St Irenaeus, whom the Church honours today, followed Christ wherever he went. Born in Smyrna in Asia Minor around the year 130, he heard as a boy the preaching of St Polycarp, who had known St John the Apostle. He went to Gaul, became a priest of Lyons, and after the bishop Pothinus died in the persecution of 177 he became bishop there himself. Against the Gnostics, who claimed a secret knowledge and despised the body and the created world, he wrote his great work Against Heresies. He taught that the true faith is the one handed on publicly by the apostles through the bishops who succeeded them, above all in the Church of Rome, founded, he wrote, by the two most glorious apostles Peter and Paul. He loved the body God created and the flesh the Word took on; he wrote that the glory of God is a human being fully alive. Tradition honours him as a martyr, and in 2022 Pope Francis declared him a Doctor of the Church with the title Doctor of Unity. Like Abraham, he stood before God for others; like the disciples, he left home to follow Christ to the ends of the known world. And tonight, with the Vigil of Sts Peter and Paul, the Church begins to celebrate the very apostles whose teaching he guarded.
outline: Ask: when you pray for others, do you give up quickly, or do you stand before God and keep asking?
Point 1 · Abraham stands before the Lord
God shares his plan with his friend, and Abraham intercedes for a sinful city.
Point 2 · For the sake of ten
A few righteous can protect many; one righteous man saves all.
Point 3 · Nowhere to lay his head
Following Jesus comes before comfort and before every other duty.
Point 4 · St Irenaeus, Doctor of Unity
A follower of Christ who guarded the apostles' faith and the goodness of creation.
“Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?”
live: Choose one place, your town, a broken family, a troubled country, and pray for it today with Abraham's humility and persistence.
Name one thing you keep postponing that Jesus is asking of you, a confession, a reconciliation, a commitment, and do it this week.
saints: Born in Smyrna in Asia Minor, a disciple of St Polycarp, who had known St John the Apostle. A priest of Lyons in Gaul, and its bishop after the persecution of 177. In Against Heresies he defended the faith handed down by the apostles through the bishops in succession, especially the Church of Rome, against Gnostic teachers who despised the body. He taught that Christ sums up and renews all creation, and that Mary's obedience undid Eve's disobedience. Honoured as a martyr; declared a Doctor of the Church, the Doctor of Unity, by Pope Francis in 2022.
2027-06-28.prayer: O God, who called the Bishop Saint Irenaeus to confirm true doctrine and peace in the Church, grant, we pray, through his intercession, that, being renewed in faith and charity, we may always be intent on fostering unity and concord. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord God, Judge of all the earth, you are merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love. Give us Abraham's courage to stand before you for our cities and our families, and the readiness of true disciples to follow your Son without delay. Through the prayers of St Irenaeus, keep us faithful to the faith of the apostles Peter and Paul. Amen.
altar: At every Mass the priest prays for the Church spread throughout the world, together with the Pope and the bishop, and for all the living and the dead. Like Abraham, the Church stands before the Lord for the whole world. But she does not plead with empty hands: she offers the one sacrifice of the one righteous Man, Jesus Christ, for whose sake God forgives not ten cities but all who turn to him. St Irenaeus wrote that the Church offers to God the first fruits of his creation, bread and wine, which become the Body and Blood of Christ.

quick: The Lord shares his plan with Abraham, and Abraham pleads for Sodom: will God sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
Abraham bargains from fifty righteous down to ten, and God agrees each time to forgive the city for their sake.
Jesus warns would-be followers that the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head and that the call of the kingdom comes first.
2027-06-28.action: Pray for your town or village today with Abraham's persistence.
2027-06-28.question: Do I give up quickly when I pray for others, or do I stand before the Lord?
kidsaint: When Irenaeus was a boy in a city called Smyrna, he listened to a holy old bishop named Polycarp, who had known St John, the friend of Jesus. Irenaeus never forgot what he heard. He travelled far away to France and became bishop of Lyons. Some people were teaching strange secret ideas and saying that our bodies and God's world are bad. Irenaeus wrote big books to explain the true faith of the apostles: God made the world good, and Jesus became a real man to save us. Lesson: hold on to the faith handed down to you, and share it clearly and kindly.

family.explain: Abraham was God's friend. When God said that the city of Sodom was very wicked, Abraham prayed for the city. He asked: if there are fifty good people there, will you save it? God said yes. Then he asked for forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty, and even ten! Each time God said yes. God loves it when we pray for others and keep on asking.
family.intention: We pray for our town or village, for our country, and for anyone we know who is far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “For which place or which person shall our family pray every night this week, like Abraham?”

illus: In a small town in central Kerala, an elderly widow was known in the parish for one thing: every evening at six she knelt on her veranda facing the road and prayed the rosary aloud for the whole street, house by house, naming each family, Christian, Hindu and Muslim alike. When she died, a Muslim neighbour came to the funeral and told the priest: we always knew someone was praying for us at six o'clock; now who will stand before God for our street? The priest thought of Abraham: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just? (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, merciful and gracious, teach us to stand before you for others, and to follow your Son wherever he goes. Amen.
share: Abraham remained standing before the Lord (Genesis 18:22). For whom is God asking me to stand before him in prayer?
Let me take it upon myself to speak to the Lord, I who am but dust and ashes (Genesis 18:27). How do humility and boldness come together in my prayer?
Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead (Matthew 8:22). What am I putting before the call of Jesus?
pm.resp: The Lord is kind and merciful.
interc: For the Church, that following St Irenaeus she may guard the faith of the apostles in unity and peace.
For our towns and cities, especially places of violence and injustice against the poor and the stranger, that God may spare them and convert hearts.
For bishops and theologians, that they may teach the truth clearly and lovingly.
For all who are discerning a call to the priesthood or religious life, that they may follow Christ without delay.
For our group, that we may become persistent intercessors for our neighbourhood.
pm.close: Father, for the sake of your righteous Son you forgive the many. Hear the prayers we make for others, and keep us faithful to the faith of Peter and Paul. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, God says something beautiful in today's first reading: shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do? (Genesis 18:17). God treats Abraham as a friend, and tells him that he is going down to see the sin of Sodom. And Abraham does what friends of God do. He does not say: good, they deserve it. He stays standing before the Lord, and he prays for the city.

Listen to his prayer. Will you indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked? Suppose there are fifty righteous. And when God agrees, he goes on: forty-five? forty? thirty? twenty? ten? He calls himself dust and ashes, but he does not stop. And each time God says yes. God is more ready to forgive than Abraham is to ask. The prayer of a righteous person, even for a wicked city, is precious to God.

This is a lesson for us. We complain a lot about our towns, our politics, our young people. Do we pray for them as much as we complain? Abraham stopped at ten. But God found one righteous man, Jesus, and for his sake he forgives all who turn to him. When we pray for others, we stand beside Jesus, the great intercessor.

In the Gospel Jesus tells those who want to follow him: the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head (Matthew 8:20). St Irenaeus, whom we honour today, took that seriously. He left his home in Asia, went to the far west, served the Church in Lyons in a time of persecution, and spent his life guarding the faith handed down from the apostles. He said: the glory of God is a human being fully alive. Today let us be fully alive in prayer for others, and in following Jesus without delay. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham was God's friend. One day God told him that a city called Sodom was very, very bad. Abraham did not say: good, punish them! He prayed for them. He asked God: if there are fifty good people, will you save the city? Then forty? Thirty? Ten? And God said yes every time! When you hear about people doing wrong, do not just say they are bad. Pray for them, like Abraham!

intro: Theme: “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?”
Abraham's bold intercession, the cost of following Jesus, and St Irenaeus, who stood for the faith of the apostles.

points.apply: Each evening this week, before your own needs, pray for one town, one family and one person far from God.

sub: God more ready to forgive than we are to ask.
q: Then he said, “Oh do not let the Lord be angry if I speak just once more. Suppose ten are found there.” He answered, “For the sake of ten I will not destroy it.”
For just as by the one man's disobedience the many were made sinners, so by the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous.
points.apply: Be one of the righteous in your street: do one act of honesty or kindness each day this week that no one asks of you.

sub: Let the dead bury their own dead.
St Irenaeus leaves all to guard the faith.
q: He left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “Let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you.”
And Jesus said to him, “Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
points.apply: Do this week the one thing you have been postponing that Jesus is clearly asking of you.

concl: Abraham shows that God wants friends who stand before him for others, and that he is more ready to forgive than we are to ask.
Jesus asks disciples who will follow him first of all, like St Irenaeus, who left his homeland and gave his life to keep the faith of the apostles.
2027-06-28.resolve: Pray each day this week for your town or village, and do without delay what Jesus asks of you.
